mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the empty set (∅) with a non‑empty set?

options.A: The empty set is a subset of every set, including non‑empty sets.
options.B: The empty set has the same cardinality as any non‑empty set.
options.C: The empty set is a proper superset of any non‑empty set.
options.D: The empty set contains at least one element that is also in any non‑empty set.

mcqs.answer: The empty set is a subset of every set, including non‑empty sets.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, ∅ ⊆ X for every set X, because there is no element in ∅ that violates the subset condition. Hence statement A is true. Statements B, C, and D are false: ∅ has cardinality 0, cannot be a superset, and contains no elements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets is a finite set?

options.B: The set of prime numbers less than 20.
options.C: The set of all points on a straight line.
options.D: The set of all real numbers between 0 and 1.

mcqs.answer: The set of prime numbers less than 20.
mcqs.explanation: A finite set contains a limited number of elements. The primes less than 20 are {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19} – eight elements – so the set is finite. Options A, C, and D describe infinite collections.

mcqs.question: An infinite set can be defined as a set that:

options.B: Can be placed in a one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself.

mcqs.answer: Can be placed in a one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself.
mcqs.explanation: A hallmark of infinite sets is that they can be put into a bijection with a proper subset of themselves (e.g., ℕ and the even numbers). Option A describes the empty set, C a singleton, and D is unrelated to infiniteness.

mcqs.question: Which description best defines a singleton set?

options.A: A set containing exactly one element.
options.C: A set containing infinitely many elements.

mcqs.answer: A set containing exactly one element.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a singleton set has precisely one member, e.g., {5}. The other options describe the empty set, an infinite set, and a two‑element set respectively.

mcqs.question: Two sets A and B are said to be equal if:

options.A: They contain exactly the same elements, irrespective of order or repetition.
options.B: They have the same number of elements.
options.C: One is a subset of the other.
options.D: They share at least one common element.

mcqs.answer: They contain exactly the same elements, irrespective of order or repetition.
mcqs.explanation: Equality of sets requires identical membership: every element of A is in B and vice‑versa. Mere cardinality equality (B), subset relation (C), or a single common element (D) are insufficient.

mcqs.question: Which pair of sets are equivalent (i.e., have the same cardinality)?

options.B: {x | x is a natural number less than 5} and {a,b,c,d}

mcqs.explanation: Equivalent sets have the same number of elements. Both sets in option C contain four elements, so they are equivalent. Option A has 3 vs 4 elements, B has 4 vs 4 but the first description actually yields 4 elements (0‑4) – however the wording may cause ambiguity; option C is unambiguous. Option D involves empty sets, which are also equivalent, but the question expects a non‑empty example, and C is the clearest choice.

mcqs.question: Which of the following descriptions correctly represents the empty set?

options.A: The set of all integers greater than 0 and less than 0.
options.C: The set of all natural numbers.
options.D: The set of all letters in the English alphabet.

mcqs.answer: The set of all integers greater than 0 and less than 0.
mcqs.explanation: No integer can be simultaneously greater than 0 and less than 0, so the described collection has no elements, i.e., it is the empty set (∅). Options B, C, and D each contain elements.

mcqs.question: In a classroom there are 30 students. Which description below represents a finite set?

options.A: The set of all possible real numbers.
options.B: The set of all students present today.
options.C: The set of all points on a line segment.

mcqs.answer: The set of all students present today.
mcqs.explanation: A finite set has a countable, limited number of elements. The class of 30 students meets this definition. Options A, C, and D describe infinite collections.
